items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Ovie had lived with Billy Taylor whom everybody called Hoss at the same time as Mack Walker and I had lived in the same appartment, so I knew Ovie well.

ctx.x: I took my horn out and started warming up and take my place on the bandstand. We always played a few sets before the show came on, so Teddy called three numbers and when he gave the starting beat on the first number which was one that I had to read because I had not memorised my part, I couldn't even see the part. The notes started running together and I could not play 8 bars of the tune. I didn't feel drink when I got on the bandstand, but my mind just wouldn't function. My fingers wouldn't move and I couldn't…

Teddy asked me what was wrong and I told him about the recording session with Fats and how much I had drunk. We called Teddy 'Fess' as so many other orchestra leaders were called. So after hearing my story, Fess told me to go out and get some air for a while and come back later. I went out for half an. hour and came back, but I was not feeling any better as far as being able to play was concerned. So Fess told me to take the night off. I had seen a trumpet player named Ovie Alston going into the bar of Big John's…

I went into Big John's, saw Ovie and told him my troubles and asked him to finish the night for me. In that manner, Teddy's band was not without a third trumpet. I made it home without staggering and went to sleep as soon as I got undressed and into bed. And I had learned a lesson that I never forget, and that was never try and drink as much as Thomas "Fats" Waller. The next session I did with him, I drank, but not every time the bottle was passed to me.
